newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba signals unhappiness over Helms-Burton deal.
newsitem.headline: Cuba signals unhappiness over Helms-Burton deal.

text.p: A proposed U.S.-European deal to settle a dispute over the U.S. Helms-Burton law does not meet Cuba's objections to the law, a Cuban minister was quoted on Monday as saying.

"For Cuba, a solution between the United States and the European Union does not solve the problem of the Helms-Burton law," the official news agency Prensa Latina quoted Foreign Trade Minister Ricardo Cabrisas as saying.
But he added: "Our government prefers to wait until the accord is finalised before judging it."
Under an initial deal struck between the European Commission and Washington on Friday, the EU would suspend a complaint at the Geneva-based World Trade Organisation.
The White House would in exchange seek to change a key provision of Helms-Burton barring executives of companies that invest in expropriated property in Cuba from entering the United States.
Meeting on Monday, European states agreed to postpone the planned WTO complaint but left until Wednesday more considered reaction to the tentative deal.

Helms-Burton, a toughening of Washington's 35-year-old economic embargo against Cuba, was passed in March 1996 after Cuban fighter planes shot down two small private U.S. planes off Cuba, killing the four Cuban-American crew members.

International criticism of the law focused on Titles Three and Four of the law that seek to deter foreign investment by punishing firms investing on property nationalised after President Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution.

Cuba has welcomed this international opposition, but also views as unacceptable other parts of the law that call for a radical political overhaul in Cuba as a condition for normalised relations with the United States.
